description.narrative: This project aims to strengthen key institutions and accountability mechanisms and reduce the scope for corruption across relevant state institutions and sectors of the economy. The overarching project goal is to significantly reduce corruption risks in emergency response funding through:• tailormade anti-corruption interventions in 11 countries by strengthening key institutions at national and multilateral levels to reduce the scope of corruption; • holding corrupt actors accountable for abuse of COVID-19 related support.The chapters will identify specific corruption risks/vulnerabilities in their national contexts and address concrete instances of suspected corruption. title.narrative: BRIDGEGAP - Bridging the Gaps in Evidence, Regulation and Impact of Anticorruption Policies

description.narrative: The BRIDGEGAP project seeks to fill critical knowledge gaps on the extent to which corruption infiltrates open societies, including through cross-border mechanisms, and on how transparency can be strengthened to counter these risks. By combining measurement, case study analysis, and practical solutions, the project aims to generate new evidence on how different types of transparency, e.g. legal (de jure) and practical (de facto), shape opportunities for corruption and the capacity of civil society to demand accountability(Specific Objective WP5) To map and measure the deficit of both legal and real transparency in EU-27 and neighbourhood countries, to clarify the interaction between transparency—both classical and digital—and citizen e-participation in order to design and adjust transparency policies for more effective preventive anticorruption policies at both member state and EU levelTI-S is involved in 3 Work Packages: leading WP5 and contributing to WP1 and WP9.Our responsibilities under WP1 consisted in overall coordination and delivery of the BRIDGEGAP Data Hub and is completed - the output was delivered in 2024. TI-S leads WP5 and is individually responsible for deliverable D5.3: conducting a case study analysis of fifteen EU member states, to identify the enabling and disabling conditions for transparency, particularly in relation to civil society's role in curbing political corruption and fostering social trust. This task is implemented in collaboration with TI chapters. The implementation was originally scheduled to start in 2024; however, administrative constraints prevented TI-S from formally engaging the TI chapters. After the Grant was amended, TI-S signed between August and September 2025 Cooperation Agreements with the 15 Chapters and implementation of WP5 started. Chapters started working in their two main deliverables in August 2025: the case study itself and the data collection or update of their respective Integrity Watch platforms. For that, Chapters received an initial financial installment 80% of their budget allocated to this project. D5.3 needs to be submitted to the Coordinator on 31.12.2026.On WP9, there are currently uncertainties regarding TI-S’s role since the task description is quite vague and there is little in indication on role division. LUISS wanted TI-S to lead deliverable D9.3 which is a Report on impact of EU anticorruption prevention regulation. This was not agreed at the project design phase nor budgeted at TI-S. Therefore, we rejected that suggestion and offered to support the data analysis and the report elaboration.Donor - European Research Executive Agency (EREA) via Lisbon Council for Economic CompetitivenessValue of the contract is 603,750 Euros

title.narrative: Countering Opaque Negotiations and Confidentiality in PRC’s External Agreements and Lending (CONCEAL)

description.narrative: Through a dual approach of evidence generation and targeted advocacy at both national and global levels, the project aims to counter the use of confidentiality clauses in borrowing agreements by China, and others lenders such as the Islamic Development Bank and France. By strengthening domestic transparency, TI seeks to reduce opportunities for corruption in debt acquisition and management. The project will draw on a set of case studies from countries currently at risk of debt distress: Malawi, Sri Lanka and Venezuela. These case studies will highlight China’s and other creditors’ hidden debt practices across different governance, economic, and strategic contexts. Building on this evidence, the project will implement a global advocacy strategy to influence reforms while simultaneously supporting national-level efforts to limit the use of confidentiality clauses in lending agreements. title.narrative: Capacity Building Programme on Social Accountability and Social Activism (Youth Act)

description.narrative: GENERAL OBJECTIVE: To promote social accountability and the safe participation of young activists in democratic life and in the fight against corruption, promoting a culture of transparency and accountability.SPECIFIC OBJECTIVES: 1- Train young activists in Latin America in democratic culture and in research and social auditing methodologies, with a practical and advocacy approach, so that they can demand accountability and safely influence public affairs in their communities.2. Promote the exchange of experiences, interaction and collaboration among young activists committed to public life, transparency and accountability, by supporting them in their research and using educational tools that allow them to transfer the knowledge they have learned to their peers or partners in their communities.MAIN ACTIVITIES Each training in social auditing will be a free training course consisting of three online workshops and a face-to-face meeting, at least one of which will be held at the Spanish Cooperation Training Centre in Santa Cruz (CFSCZ).Each Training will have a total duration of approximately 100 hours, and will be taught by Transparency International with the support of professors from the Complutense University of Madrid (UCM). The latter will teach approximately 30 hours of the total itinerary.The overall approach to the training will be practical so that, with the skills learned, young people can implement research, demand accountability and put into practice advocacy strategies in their municipalities, communities or neighbourhoods in a safe manner. Young people will have specialised mentoring at key moments of the training process and afterwards so that, once the training has finished, they can successfully implement their research.The training will last approximately 5 months, with each workshop taking place over four/five weeks. The modules will be a combination of synchronous and asynchronous sessions. As part of the training itinerary, participants are expected to carry out practical work at home, which will count as part of the training.The online training workshops will be held on the Intercoonecta platform and will cover the following topics: 1) theoretical bases of democracy, participation, human rights and the fight against corruption and case studies, 2) research methodologies and social auditing and 3) advocacy strategies and strategic communication.The workshops will include theoretical presentations, technical tutorials, practical workshops and inspiring masterclasses, as well as other dynamic and innovative methodologies. They will feature the participation of regionally and globally recognized professors, experts and activists from the Complutense University of Madrid, the global network of Transparency International and other relevant institutions.Throughout the training communities of practice will be formed, grouped by themes selected based on the research and projects of the young people, in order to facilitate discussions and exchanges. Among the practical work that the young participants will carry out, it is planned to implement a standardized virtual survey for their peers about their experience with democracy and the impact of the lack of transparency in key areas of community life. This task will serve to articulate the first and second workshops and its results will be condensed into a document that can be published at the end of the two editions of the training itinerary.In both face-to-face meetings, the young participants will be able to deepen the application of the knowledge learned virtually to their specific cases, in a practical way and with the support of tutors. The methodological design of the meeting will take into account the communities of practice created in the virtual phase, so that participants can exchange and implement relevant tools for their research, as well as bring others to the table. In turn, the meeting will provide “trainer of trainers” content so that participants can multiply the scope of the action after the training. The face-to-face meetings will be essential to strengthen the communities of practice and the creation of a network of young social auditors that promotes the exchange of experiences, interaction and collaboration between young people from different Latin American countries committed to public life and the fight against corruption in their communities.COUNTRIES INVOLVED ARE:Argentina, Brazil, Chile, Peru, Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador, Venezuela, Panama, Costa Rica, Honduras, Guatemala, Mexico, Dominican Republic. title.narrative: Integrity Pacts EU Helpdesk

description.narrative: "Supporting multi-stakeholder action to safeguard the EU Cohesion Policy” aims to contribute to the effective deployment of IPs in procurement projects funded by the European Regional Development Fund (ERDF), Cohesion Fund, or Just Transition Fund (JTF) in interested Member States. The action targets Managing Authorities, intermediate bodies, contracting authorities, and CSOs, focusing on countries with high potential for IP implementation in the short term. The proposed action has three specific objectives:Objective 1 – Enhance IP stakeholders’ (MAs, intermediate bodies, contracting authorities, CSOs) awareness of and access to policy guidance, technical assistance, and knowledge resources to strategically apply IPs to relevant EU-funded projects. This will be done through 1) the development of an online IP Helpdesk platform facilitating ad-hoc assistance on specific IP projects, and 2) the development of policy guidance for the application of the IP to the Cohesion Policy Funds spending cycle based on a new, global blueprint for IP implementation developed by TI (see section b for more details).Objective 2 – Strengthen the capacity of local CSOs to initiate, prepare, execute, and scale-up the IPs for EU-funded projects in collaboration with public and private sector actors. This will be done by 1) providing training on IP set-up and implementation as well as related advocacy, capacity-building, and awareness-raising activities, and 2) providing support for targeted civil society actions to boost preparation or implementation of concrete IPs in countries with high potential (see section b). Objective 3 – Foster cross-country coordination, peer-learning, and community building on the strategic deployment of IPs to safeguard EU Cohesion Policy programmes. This will be done by convening MAs, CSOs, as well as key EU oversight institutions (e.g., DGs, OLAF, ECA, EPPO) in online sessions to discuss common approaches to IP application to ERDF, CF, and JTF projects in critical sector/policy areas both in the current and next EU budget cycle.Value of the contract EUR 300,000.
